question: A shop's quarterly sales (₹ lakh): Q1 = 40, Q2 = 52, Q3 = 48, Q4 = 60. Between which two consecutive quarters was the percentage growth the highest?
d: Both Q1 to Q2 and Q3 to Q4, since each rose by ₹12 lakh
why: Q1 to Q2 is 12/40 = 30%, Q3 to Q4 is 12/48 = 25%. The rupee rise is equal but the base differs.

question: Four bus routes: R1 has 120 seats with 90 passengers, R2 has 80 seats with 66 passengers, R3 has 150 seats with 105 passengers, R4 has 60 seats with 48 passengers. Which route has the highest percentage of seats occupied?
why: Occupancy: R1 75%, R2 82.5%, R3 70%, R4 80%. R3 carries the most people but has the lowest share.

question: Daily units sold, Monday to Thursday. Store X: 120, 150, 90, 140. Store Y: 100, 130, 110, 170. By what percentage does Y's four-day total exceed X's four-day total?
why: X totals 500 and Y totals 510. The excess is 10 on a base of 500 (X), so 2%.

question: Three sections took a test. Section A: 30 students, average 62. Section B: 20 students, average 70. Section C: 50 students, average 58. What is the average over all 100 students?
why: Weighted mean = (30×62 + 20×70 + 50×58)/100 = 6160/100 = 61.6. The simple mean of 62, 70 and 58 is 63.33, which is the trap.

question: Revenue = price × units. Compared with the previous year, price changed by +20% in 2022, −10% in 2023 and +25% in 2024; units sold changed by −10% in 2022, +30% in 2023 and −20% in 2024. Revenue in 2021 was ₹50 lakh. What was the revenue in 2024?

Four towns (population in lakh; share of males; male literacy; female literacy): P (10; 55%; 80%; 60%), Q (8; 50%; 90%; 70%), R (12; 60%; 75%; 50%), S (6; 52%; 85%; 80%). Which town has the highest overall literacy rate?
why: Overall rate = male share × male literacy + female share × female literacy: P 71%, Q 80%, R 65%, S 82.6%. Q has the best male literacy but S wins overall.

question: Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north, in positions 1 to 5 from the left. Conditions: C is somewhere to the left of E; E is immediately to the left of A; A is immediately to the left of B; C and E are not next to each other. Who sits in the middle (position 3)?
why: Placing the conditions gives the order C D E A B from the left, so E is in the middle.

question: Five friends A, B, C, D and E sit in a row facing north, in positions 1 to 5 from the left. Conditions: A and C are not next to each other; D is immediately to the left of E; exactly 2 people sit between C and E; C is somewhere to the left of D. Who sits at the extreme right (position 5)?
why: The order from the left is C B D E A, so A is at the extreme right.

question: Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. Conditions: A sits opposite C; D and E are not neighbours; D sits immediately to the left of C; A and B are not neighbours. Who sits opposite B?
why: Placing the conditions gives the clockwise order A E B C D F, so F is opposite B.

question: Six people P, Q, R, S, T and U sit in a row, positions 1 to 6 from the left. Conditions: U is somewhere to the left of Q; T is immediately to the left of Q; exactly 2 people sit between S and T; R is somewhere to the left of U; exactly 1 person sits between R and U. Who sits in position 4 from the left?
why: The row from the left is R S U P T Q, so P is fourth.

question: Eight friends A to H live on different floors of an eight-floor building, the ground floor being floor 1 and the top floor being floor 8. Conditions: G is somewhere below H; C and H are not on adjacent floors; C is immediately below D; H is somewhere below D; G is immediately below F; F is immediately below E; B is somewhere below F. Who lives on floor 5?
why: The floors from the ground upwards are B G F E H A C D, so floor 5 is H.

question: Eight friends A to H sit around a circular table, all facing the centre. Conditions: C sits opposite D; B and F are not neighbours; C and E are not neighbours; F sits second to the left of D; G sits second to the left of C; B and D are not neighbours; H sits second to the left of A. Who sits second to the left of G?
why: Placing the conditions gives the clockwise order A F H C B G E D. Facing the centre, left is clockwise, so second to the left of G is D.

question: Four boxes P, Q, R and S hold 28 balls in all. P has 2 more balls than Q. Q has 1 fewer ball than R. R has twice as many balls as S. How many balls are in P?
why: Let S = s: R = 2s, Q = 2s − 1, P = 2s + 1. The total 7s = 28 gives s = 4, so P = 9.

question: Asha, Bala and Chitra bought apples, mangoes and bananas (number of fruits). Row totals: Asha 15, Bala 12, Chitra 18. Column totals: apples 14, mangoes 16, bananas 15. Known: Asha bought 5 apples and 6 mangoes; Bala bought 4 apples and 3 bananas. How many bananas did Chitra buy?
why: Asha's bananas = 4, Bala's mangoes = 5. Chitra's bananas = 15 − 4 − 3 = 8, and her total checks: 5 + 5 + 8 = 18.

question: Six players A to F each scored a different value from 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 in a game. Clues: C scored exactly 20 more than D; F scored 20; B scored exactly 20 more than E; E scored 10. How many did A score?
why: B = 30 and F = 20 follow from the clues, leaving 40, 50 and 60. C is exactly 20 more than D, which only works as C = 60 and D = 40, so A = 50.

question: A trader sells three products in three cities (units). Row totals: Pune 14, Surat 16, Indore 15. Column totals: shirts 13, caps 17, belts 15. Known cells: Pune-shirts 3, Pune-belts 5, Surat-shirts 5, Indore-caps 4. How many caps were sold in Surat?
why: Pune-caps = 14 − 3 − 5 = 6. Surat-caps and Surat-belts add to 16 − 5 = 11, and caps total 17 gives Indore-caps 4, so Surat-caps = 17 − 6 − 4 = 7.

question: A 4×4 grid is filled with the digits 1 to 4 so that every row and every column has each digit exactly once. Given: Row 1: _ _ _ _ | Row 2: _ 1 _ _ | Row 3: _ _ 2 3 | Row 4: _ _ 3 _. Also, the entry in row 4, column 1 is larger than the entry in row 4, column 2; the entry in row 3, column 2 is larger than the entry in row 3, column 3. What is the entry in row 1, column 4?
why: Fill forced cells first using the row and column rule, then use the two inequality clues to settle the remaining choice. The grid has exactly one completion.

question: Ten identical laddoos are given to four children Anu, Binu, Charu and Dev. Each child gets at least 1 laddoo, Anu gets at most 3, and Dev gets more laddoos than Binu. In how many ways can this be done?
why: Fix Anu = 1, 2 or 3, then count the splits of the rest among Binu, Charu and Dev (each at least 1) with Dev > Binu. Adding the three cases gives the total.

question: In a knockout tournament, a team that loses a match is out. There are 13 teams. How many matches are played in all to decide the champion?
why: Every match removes exactly one team, and 12 teams must be removed to leave one champion, so 12 matches.

question: Seven teams play a league in which every team plays every other team twice (once at home, once away). How many matches are played in all?
why: Pairs of teams = 7×6/2 = 21, and each pair meets twice, so 42.

question: Five teams A, B, C, D and E play a league in which each pair meets once. A win earns 2 points, a draw 1 point each and a loss 0. At the end A has 7 points, B has 6, C has 4 and D has 2. How many points does E have?
why: There are 10 matches and every match hands out 2 points in total, so 20 points. E = 20 − (7 + 6 + 4 + 2) = 1.

question: Six players A to F play a chess round-robin: each pair plays one game, a win scores 1 point, a draw 0.5 each and a loss 0. Final scores: A 4, B 3.5, C 3, D 2.5, E 1.5. What did F score?
why: 15 games give 15 points in all. F = 15 − (4 + 3.5 + 3 + 2.5 + 1.5) = 0.5.

question: Five teams A, B, C, D and E play a round-robin: each pair plays once and there are no draws. Final wins: A 3, B 2, C 2, D 2, E 1. Further known results: A beat D; E beat B; C beat D. Which team beat A?
why: Using the wins column and the known results, all 10 matches are forced; the only team that beat A is B.

question: Six teams A to F play a round-robin: each pair plays once and there are no draws. Final wins: A 4, B 3, C 3, D 2, E 2, F 1. Further known results: C beat F; A beat B; C beat E; C beat B; A beat E; A beat F. Which team beat A?
why: A won 4 of its 5 games, so it lost exactly one. Combining the win counts with the known results fixes every match, and the only team that beat A is D.

question: Roads between towns (km): A–B 7, A–C 4, B–D 5, C–D 9, C–E 12, D–E 3, B–E 11. All roads are two-way. What is the shortest distance from A to E?
why: A–B–D–E = 7 + 5 + 3 = 15 km. A–C–D–E and A–C–E are both 16 km.

question: One-way roads: A→B, A→C, B→C, B→D, C→D, C→E, D→E. How many different routes lead from A to E?
why: Count routes by last stop: routes to E = routes to C + routes to D. Routes to B = 1, to C = 2, to D = routes(B)+routes(C) = 3, so E = 2 + 3 = 5.

question: Two-way roads (km): P–Q 6, P–R 11, Q–R 4, Q–S 8, R–S 6, R–T 10, S–T 3, Q–T 14. A courier must go from P to T and must pass through R on the way. What is the shortest possible distance?
why: Best route through R: P–Q–R–S–T = 6 + 4 + 6 + 3 = 19 km. The unconstrained shortest route, P–Q–S–T (17 km), skips R.

question: A metro has three lines. Red: P, Q, R, S, T. Blue: U, R, V, W. Green: X, T, W, Y. Lines meet at stations they share (R is on Red and Blue, T on Red and Green, W on Blue and Green). What is the minimum number of train changes needed to travel from P to Y?
why: P is on Red only and Y on Green only. Red meets Green directly at T, so one change at T is enough.

question: Two-way roads, each shown as (distance in km, toll in ₹): H–A (10, 40), H–B (15, 10), A–C (12, 30), B–C (25, 5), B–D (20, 20), C–D (8, 0), A–D (30, 10). A truck goes from H to D without visiting any town twice, and the total distance must be at most 40 km. What is the lowest total toll it can pay?
why: Routes within 40 km: H–A–C–D (30 km, ₹70), H–B–D (35 km, ₹30) and H–A–D (40 km, ₹50). The cheapest route overall, H–B–C–D (₹15), is 48 km, so it is too long.

question: A city has three train lines. Line 1: station 1 to 2 takes 6 min, 2 to 3 takes 10 min, 3 to 4 takes 12 min. Line 2: station 2 to 5 takes 5 min, 5 to 4 takes 9 min. Line 3: station 1 to 5 takes 12 min. Every change of line costs 5 minutes of waiting. All lines run both ways. What is the shortest time from station 1 to station 4?
why: Line 1 all the way takes 28. Line 3 to station 5 then Line 2 takes 12 + 5 + 9 = 26. Line 1 to station 2, change, then Line 2 takes 6 + 5 + 5 + 9 = 25. Forgetting the 5-minute wait gives 20.

question: A technician starts at 9:00 am. Task A takes 40 min, then Task B takes 25 min, then he takes a 15-minute break, then Task C takes 55 min and Task D takes 30 min. At what time does he finish?

Rohit is free 9:00–11:00 and 14:00–17:00. Sana is free 10:00–12:00 and 13:00–16:00. Tej is free 10:30–13:30 and 15:00–18:00. They need a one-hour meeting at a time when all three are free. What is the earliest start time?
why: Common time: 10:30–11:00 (only 30 min) and 15:00–16:00 (60 min). So the earliest one-hour slot starts at 15:00.

question: A bank has two counters. Customers join one common queue in order of arrival and go to whichever counter is free (counter 1 if both are free). Arrival time (minutes after opening) and service time: C1 (0, 6), C2 (1, 8), C3 (2, 4), C4 (3, 5), C5 (4, 3). At what minute does the last customer finish?
why: C1 uses counter 1 (0–6) and C2 counter 2 (1–9). C3 gets counter 1 (6–10). C4 gets counter 2 (9–14). C5 gets counter 1 (10–13). The last finish is at minute 14.

question: Five exams (Chemistry, English, History, Maths, Physics) are held on five consecutive days, Monday to Friday, one per day. Conditions: Physics is on the day immediately before English; History is on an earlier day than English; exactly 2 days separate Chemistry and Physics; Chemistry is on the day immediately before History. Which exam is on Wednesday?
why: The conditions fix the order Chemistry → History → Maths → Physics → English from Monday to Friday, so Wednesday has Maths.

question: Two workers must finish six jobs; a job cannot be split and a worker does one job at a time. Durations (hours) and what must finish first: A 3 (none), B 2 (after A), C 4 (none), D 2 (after B and C), E 3 (after A), F 2 (after D and E). What is the least time in which all six jobs can be finished?
why: The chain A → B → D → F takes 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 9 hours and cannot be shortened. Total work is 16 hours, which would give 8 on two workers, but the chain forces 9 and 9 is achievable.

question: Seven candidates Arjun, Bhavna, Chetan, Divya, Esha, Farhan and Gauri are interviewed one per day on seven consecutive days, Monday to Sunday. Conditions: Gauri is on the day immediately before Divya; Esha is on an earlier day than Gauri; Divya is on the day immediately before Chetan; Chetan is on the day immediately before Bhavna; Arjun and Esha are not on consecutive days; exactly 1 day separates Arjun and Divya. Who is interviewed on Friday?
why: The conditions fix the order Esha → Farhan → Arjun → Gauri → Divya → Chetan → Bhavna from Monday to Sunday, so Friday is Divya.

question: In a class of 120 students, 70 play cricket, 55 play football and 20 play both. How many play neither game?
why: Cricket or football = 70 + 55 − 20 = 105. Neither = 120 − 105 = 15.

question: Of 200 people surveyed, 120 drink tea, 90 drink coffee and 40 drink both. How many drink exactly one of the two?
why: Only tea = 120 − 40 = 80 and only coffee = 90 − 40 = 50, so exactly one = 130.

question: In a group of 100 people, 60 like A, 50 like B and 40 like C. 25 like both A and B, 15 like both B and C, 20 like both A and C, and 10 like all three. How many like exactly two of the three?
why: The pair counts (25, 15, 20) each include the 10 who like all three. Exactly two = (25 + 15 + 20) − 3×10 = 30.

question: In a group of 100 people, 70 own a bike, 80 own a phone and 90 own a laptop. What is the minimum possible number of people who own all three?
why: People missing at least one item: at most 30 + 20 + 10 = 60. So at least 100 − 60 = 40 own all three.

question: A store has 110 customers. 70 bought X, 55 bought Y and 45 bought Z. 10 bought all three. 25 bought both X and Y (including those who bought all three) and 20 bought both Y and Z (including those who bought all three). How many bought only Y?
why: Y buyers = only Y + (XY only) + (YZ only) + all three. XY only = 25 − 10 = 15 and YZ only = 20 − 10 = 10. So only Y = 55 − 15 − 10 − 10 = 20.

question: In a town of 800 people, 60% read newspaper A, 50% read B and 40% read C. 30% read both A and B, 20% read both B and C, 25% read both A and C, and 10% read all three. How many people read exactly one of the three newspapers?
why: By inclusion–exclusion the readers of at least one paper are 60 + 50 + 40 − 30 − 20 − 25 + 10 = 85%. Readers of at least two are 75 − 2×10 = 55%. Exactly one = 85 − 55 = 30% of 800 = 240.

question: A father is 4 times as old as his son. After 6 years he will be 3 times as old as the son. What is the father's present age?
why: Let the son be s: 4s + 6 = 3(s + 6), so s = 12 and the father is 48.

question: Car A runs 15 km per litre of petrol costing ₹100 per litre. Car B runs 25 km per kg of CNG costing ₹80 per kg. How much less does Car B cost for a 300 km trip?

Mobile plan X costs ₹300 a month and includes 60 minutes; extra minutes cost ₹2.50 each. Plan Y costs ₹100 a month plus ₹3 per minute for every minute used. For how many minutes of use in a month do both plans cost the same? (Use more than 60 minutes.)
Raju spends 40% of his salary on rent, then 25% of what remains on food, then 20% of what remains after that on travel. He saves the rest, which is ₹21,600. What is his salary?
why: After rent 60% is left, after food 75% of that, after travel 80% of that: 0.6 × 0.75 × 0.8 = 0.36 of the salary. 21,600 / 0.36 = ₹60,000.

question: Income tax per year (₹ lakh): nil up to 3, 5% on the part from 3 to 7, 10% on the part from 7 to 10, and 20% on the part above 10. A person pays ₹1.6 lakh in tax. What is the person's income?
why: Tax up to 10 lakh = 0.05×4 + 0.10×3 = 0.5 lakh. The remaining 1.1 lakh is at 20%, so 5.5 lakh above 10. Income = 15.5 lakh.

question: Ajay invests ₹50,000 for the whole year but withdraws ₹10,000 after 8 months. Bela invests ₹40,000 and adds ₹20,000 after 5 months. At the end of the year the profit is ₹59,000. What is Ajay's share?

Monthly electricity units used by four housing societies: Pune 840 then 924, Nashik 600 then 690, Indore 500 then 545, Surat 720 then 780 (first figure is last year, second is this year). Which society showed the highest percentage increase?
why: Increases: Pune 10%, Nashik 15%, Indore 9%, Surat 8.33%. Nashik is highest, though Pune added the most units (84).

question: In a test, 30 students of Section A averaged 60 marks and 20 students of Section B averaged 80 marks. What is the average of all 50 students?
why: Total = 30x60 + 20x80 = 1800 + 1600 = 3400; 3400/50 = 68. The simple mean 70 ignores the unequal group sizes.

question: A price index of rice has base year 2020 = 100. The index for 2022 is 125. If rice cost ₹80 per kg in 2020, what did it cost in 2022?
why: An index of 125 means 25% above the base: 80 x 1.25 = ₹100 per kg.

question: Units produced by Plants X, Y and Z: Jan (120, 95, 110); Feb (100, 105, 98); Mar (130, 90, 85); Apr (115, 105, 100). In which month was the combined output of the three plants highest?
why: Monthly totals are Jan 325, Feb 303, Mar 305, Apr 320. January is highest, even though March had the best single plant (130).

question: Out of 150 customers who visited a mobile shop on Saturday, 45 bought a phone, 60 bought only accessories and the rest bought nothing. What percentage of the customers bought nothing?
why: Nothing bought = 150 - 45 - 60 = 45 customers, and 45/150 = 30%.

question: A start-up's monthly profit fell from ₹250 thousand in May to ₹200 thousand in June. By what percentage must June's profit rise in July to get back to the May level?
why: The fall is 20% of the old base 250, but the rise is on the lower base: 50/200 = 25%.

question: A course gives weights of 20% to the Quiz, 30% to the Project and 50% to the Exam. Riya scored 80 in the Quiz, 70 in the Project and 90 in the Exam. What is her weighted score?
why: 0.2x80 + 0.3x70 + 0.5x90 = 16 + 21 + 45 = 82. The plain mean of the three scores is 80, which ignores the weights.

question: A company's revenue rose 20% in 2022 over 2021 and then fell 10% in 2023 from 2022. By what percentage is the 2023 revenue above or below the 2021 revenue?
why: Take 2021 = 100. Then 2022 = 120 and 2023 = 108, so 8% above. Adding +20 and -10 gives a wrong 10%.

question: A shop sold three items. X: 40 units at ₹25 each. Y: 30 units at ₹40 each. Z: 30 units at ₹10 each. What share of the total revenue came from Y?
why: Revenue: X 1000, Y 1200, Z 300, total 2500. Y's share is 1200/2500 = 48%. Y's share of units is only 30%.

question: In a class the average height of the boys is 150 cm and of the girls 140 cm. The average height of the whole class is 144 cm. What is the ratio of boys to girls?
why: By alligation, boys : girls = (144 - 140) : (150 - 144) = 4 : 6 = 2 : 3. The overall mean sits nearer the girls' mean, so there are more girls.

question: A cost-of-living index with base 2019 = 100 reads 130 in 2021 and 156 in 2023. If 2021 is taken as the new base (=100), what is the index for 2023?
why: New index = 156/130 x 100 = 120. Subtracting 130 from 156 gives a wrong 26 points.

question: State A has a population of 40 lakh with 50% literacy. State B has 60 lakh with 70% literacy. What is the overall literacy rate of the two states together?
why: Literate people = 20 + 42 = 62 lakh out of 100 lakh, so 62%. The plain average of 50 and 70 is 60%, which ignores populations.

question: Five judges gave scores to a dancer. The mean of the five scores is 72. Four of the scores are 65, 78, 80 and 70. What is the difference between the highest and lowest of the five scores?
why: Fifth score = 5x72 - (65+78+80+70) = 360 - 293 = 67. Highest 80, lowest 65, so the difference is 15.

question: A caterer buys ₹3,000 worth of onions from Shop P at ₹20 per kg and ₹3,000 worth from Shop Q at ₹30 per kg. What is the average price per kg paid for all the onions?
why: Quantity = 150 kg + 100 kg = 250 kg for ₹6,000, so ₹24 per kg. Spending equal amounts gives the harmonic mean, not 25.

question: A class of 21 students has an average of 60 marks. When the topper, who scored 100, leaves the class, what is the average of the remaining students?
why: Total = 21x60 = 1260. Remaining = 1260 - 100 = 1160 for 20 students; 1160/20 = 58.

question: A household index is built from three groups with weights Food 40%, Rent 30% and Transport 30%. This year's group indices (base year = 100) are Food 150, Rent 120 and Transport 110. What is the combined index?
why: Weighted index = 0.4x150 + 0.3x120 + 0.3x110 = 60 + 36 + 33 = 129. The simple mean of 150, 120 and 110 is 126.67, which ignores weights.

question: The price of cooking oil rises by 25%. By what percentage must a family cut its consumption so that its monthly spending on oil stays the same?
why: New price is 1.25 times, so quantity must be 1/1.25 = 0.8 of the old, a 20% cut. A 25% cut would reduce spending.

question: Sales (₹ crore) of a company by region, 2021 then 2022. North: 200, 240. South: 300, 330. West: 500, 530. Which statement is correct?
a: West grew fastest because it added the most rupees; total sales grew 6%
b: South grew fastest at 10%; total sales grew 10%
c: North grew fastest at 20%, and total sales grew 10%
d: North grew fastest at 20%; total sales grew 8%
why: Growth: North 40/200 = 20%, South 30/300 = 10%, West 30/500 = 6%. Total 1000 to 1100 is 10%. West has the biggest base, not the biggest growth.

question: 5 friends Asha, Bilal, Chetan, Deepa and Esha sit in a row, in positions 1 to 5 from left to right, one person per position. Exactly 1 person sits between Bilal and Deepa. Bilal sits somewhere between Asha and Deepa. Bilal sits immediately to the right of Esha. Bilal sits somewhere to the right of Asha. Who sits at position 3?
why: The only order that fits every clue (position 1 to 5) is Asha, Esha, Bilal, Chetan, Deepa, so position 3 is Bilal.

question: 5 tenants Mehta, Nair, Oberoi, Paul and Qureshi each live on a different floor of a 5-storey building (floor 1 is the lowest). Qureshi lives on a floor between those of Nair and Oberoi. Paul lives on the floor immediately above Qureshi's. Exactly 2 floors lie between the floors of Qureshi and Nair. Who lives on floor 2?
why: The only order that fits every clue (position 1 to 5) is Oberoi, Qureshi, Paul, Mehta, Nair, so position 2 is Qureshi.

question: 6 friends Kabir, Leela, Mohan, Neha, Omar and Pooja sit around a round table, all facing the centre. (A person's left is the next seat clockwise.) Mohan sits second to the left of Leela. Omar sits immediately to the left of Neha. Kabir and Omar sit next to each other. Who sits exactly opposite Pooja?
why: Placing the people clockwise from Kabir gives Kabir, Leela, Pooja, Mohan, Neha, Omar; reading off that circle, the answer is Omar.

question: 5 runners Tara, Uday, Vikram, Waqar and Yash finish a race with no ties (position 1 is the first to finish). Uday finished between Tara and Yash. Waqar and Yash did not finish in consecutive places. Waqar finished after Tara. Waqar finished between Uday and Yash. Who finished in position 3?
why: The only order that fits every clue (position 1 to 5) is Tara, Uday, Waqar, Vikram, Yash, so position 3 is Waqar.

question: 6 friends Dev, Esha, Farid, Gita, Hari and Isha sit in a row, in positions 1 to 6 from left to right, one person per position. Isha and Esha sit next to each other. Hari sits at the left end. Esha sits at the right end. Dev sits immediately to the right of Farid. Farid sits immediately to the right of Hari. Who sits at position 4?
why: The only order that fits every clue (position 1 to 6) is Hari, Farid, Dev, Gita, Isha, Esha, so position 4 is Gita.

question: 5 friends Mehta, Nair, Oberoi, Paul and Qureshi sit around a round table, all facing the centre. (A person's left is the next seat clockwise.) Nair sits second to the left of Mehta. Nair and Oberoi sit next to each other. Oberoi and Paul sit next to each other. Who sits immediately to the left of Paul?
why: Placing the people clockwise from Mehta gives Mehta, Qureshi, Nair, Oberoi, Paul; reading off that circle, the answer is Mehta.

question: 6 friends Dev, Esha, Farid, Gita, Hari and Isha sit in a row, in positions 1 to 6 from left to right, one person per position. Isha sits somewhere between Dev and Gita. Hari and Esha do not sit next to each other. Exactly 4 people sit between Esha and Gita. Isha sits immediately to the right of Dev. Dev sits immediately to the right of Farid. At which position does Gita sit?
why: The only order that fits every clue (position 1 to 6) is Esha, Farid, Dev, Isha, Hari, Gita, so Gita is at position 6.

question: 6 tenants Jaya, Kunal, Lata, Manoj, Nisha and Omkar each live on a different floor of a 6-storey building (floor 1 is the lowest). Nisha lives on the floor immediately above Kunal's. Jaya and Omkar do not live on adjacent floors. Lata and Omkar do not live on adjacent floors. Nisha lives on a floor between those of Jaya and Kunal. Nisha and Jaya do not live on adjacent floors. Exactly 4 floors lie between the floors of Lata and Jaya. On which floor does Nisha live?
why: The only order that fits every clue (floor 1 to 6) is Lata, Kunal, Nisha, Omkar, Manoj, Jaya, so Nisha is at floor 3.

question: 5 runners Tara, Uday, Vikram, Waqar and Yash finish a race with no ties (position 1 is the first to finish). Waqar finished after Yash. Vikram finished between Waqar and Yash. Exactly 2 runners finished between Uday and Vikram. Exactly 1 runner finished between Yash and Waqar. Vikram finished after Tara. In which position did Yash finish?
why: The only order that fits every clue (position 1 to 5) is Uday, Tara, Yash, Vikram, Waqar, so Yash is at position 3.

question: 7 friends Anil, Bhavna, Charu, Dinesh, Eshan, Falguni and Gopal sit around a round table, all facing the centre. (A person's left is the next seat clockwise.) Gopal sits second to the left of Dinesh. Anil and Falguni do not sit next to each other. Dinesh sits immediately to the left of Eshan. Bhavna and Charu do not sit next to each other. Anil and Bhavna do not sit next to each other. Eshan and Falguni sit next to each other. Who sits immediately to the right of Dinesh?
why: Placing the people clockwise from Anil gives Anil, Charu, Falguni, Eshan, Dinesh, Bhavna, Gopal; reading off that circle, the answer is Eshan.

why: All solutions of P+Q+R+S=15 with each at least 1: C(14,3) = 364. A box with 7 or more: set it to 6 plus a positive extra, leaving C(8,3) = 56 ways per box, 4 x 56 = 224 (two boxes cannot both reach 7). 364 - 224 = 140.

question: 4 teams play a league in which each pair meets once. A win gives 3 points, a draw gives 1 point to each team and a loss gives 0. The four teams finish with 7, 4, 4 and 1 points. How many matches ended in a draw?
why: Total points = 7+4+4+1 = 16. Six matches: a decisive game gives 3 points and a draw gives 2, so 3(6 - d) + 2d = 18 - d = 16 and d = 2.

question: In a 6-team single round-robin with no draws (win = 1 point), the five teams other than Zeta finished with 4, 3, 3, 2 and 1 points. How many wins did Zeta get?
why: Total matches = 15 = total wins. The five teams have 4+3+3+2+1 = 13 wins, so Zeta has 15 - 13 = 2.

question: In a 6-team single round-robin there are no draws and a win earns 1 point. The top 4 teams qualify, and ties on points are broken by a coin toss that could go either way. What is the smallest number of wins that guarantees a team qualifies?
why: 15 matches mean 15 wins in all. Five teams can each have 3 wins (5 x 3 = 15), so 3 wins can miss out. But four teams with 4 wins would need 16 wins, which is impossible, so at most 3 teams reach 4 wins and a 4-win team is always in the top 4.

question: A knockout tournament has 100 teams. Round 1 is arranged so that round 2 has exactly 64 teams, and the teams that do not play in round 1 get a bye. How many teams get a bye in round 1?
why: Round 2 has 64 teams. Round 1 must remove 36 teams, so there are 36 matches and 72 teams play. The other 100 - 72 = 28 teams get byes.

question: 4 teams play a league where each pair meets once (win 3, draw 1, loss 0). Ties on points are broken by a coin toss that could go either way, and the top 2 teams qualify. What is the smallest number of points that guarantees qualification?
why: Three teams can finish level on 6 points (A beats B, B beats C, C beats A, and all three beat D), so 6 is not safe. Three teams cannot all reach 7, since 21 points exceed the 18 available (6 matches x 3 points). So at most 2 teams reach 7 and 7 is safe.

question: A technician does three jobs one after another: 25 minutes, 40 minutes and 15 minutes, with no break between them. If he starts at 9:20 am, when does he finish?

question: Meena is free from 10:00 to 12:00 and from 14:00 to 16:00. Naveen is free from 11:00 to 13:00 and from 15:00 to 17:00. For how many minutes in total are both free at the same time?

question: A bank has one counter that serves each customer in exactly 6 minutes. Eight customers are already in the queue when it opens, and the counter starts at once. How long does the 5th customer in the queue wait before her service begins?
why: Four customers are served before her, 4 x 6 = 24 minutes.

question: Machine P packs 15 boxes an hour and Machine Q packs 25 boxes an hour. Working together, how many hours do they need to pack 120 boxes?

question: A school day starts at 8:30 am. Every period is 45 minutes long, and there is one 10-minute break after the 2nd period only. At what time does the 4th period start?
why: Periods 1 and 2 end at 10:00; after the 10-minute break period 3 runs 10:10 to 10:55, so period 4 starts at 10:55 am.

question: A project has four tasks. A takes 3 days. B (2 days) and C (4 days) can start only after A finishes and can run at the same time. D (1 day) can start only after both B and C finish. What is the minimum number of days to finish the project?
why: The longest chain is A, C, D: 3 + 4 + 1 = 8 days. B runs alongside C and does not add time.

question: Tasks and durations in days: P 4, Q 3, R 5, S 2, T 3, U 2. Precedence: R needs P; S needs P and Q; T needs R; U needs S and T. Unlimited workers are available, so tasks with no clash run in parallel. What is the shortest time to finish all tasks?
why: Longest chain: P (4) then R (5) then T (3) then U (2) = 14 days. The chain through S is shorter.

question: Three colleagues are free at these times. Anil: 9:00-11:00 and 13:00-15:00. Bela: 9:30-10:30 and 12:00-14:30. Chirag: 10:00-10:45 and 13:45-16:00. A meeting needs all three together. What is the total time (in minutes) when all three are free?
why: Common to Anil and Bela: 9:30-10:30 and 13:00-14:30. Adding Chirag (10:00-10:45, 13:45-16:00) leaves 10:00-10:30 (30 min) and 13:45-14:30 (45 min). Total 75 minutes.

question: A clinic has 2 counters. Customers join one queue and the next customer goes to whichever counter is free first (counter 1 if both are free). Six customers arrive at minutes 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, needing 5, 3, 4, 2, 6 and 3 minutes of service. At what minute do all six customers finish?
why: Customer 1 (counter 1): 0-5. Customer 2 (counter 2): 1-4. Customer 3 (counter 2, free at 4): 4-8. Customer 4 (counter 1, free at 5): 5-7. Customer 5 (counter 1, free at 7): 7-13. Customer 6 (counter 2, free at 8): 8-11. The last to finish is at minute 13.

question: Two bus routes leave the same stop together at 7:00 am. Route 1 buses leave every 12 minutes and Route 2 buses every 18 minutes. At what time do two buses next leave together?
why: The buses coincide every LCM(12, 18) = 36 minutes, so the next common departure is 7:36 am.

question: A printer prints 5 pages a minute. After every 20 pages it must pause for 1 minute to cool, but it does not pause after the final page. How long does it take to print a 100-page document?
why: Printing takes 100/5 = 20 minutes. Pauses come after pages 20, 40, 60 and 80, which is 4 minutes. Total 24 minutes.

question: Priya can attend a workshop only on days when she is free. She is free every 3rd day starting from day 2 (days 2, 5, 8, ...). Ravi is free every 4th day starting from day 2 (days 2, 6, 10, ...). Counting day 1 as the first day, on which day do they next share a free day after day 2?
why: Priya's days leave remainder 2 when divided by 3; Ravi's leave remainder 2 when divided by 4. Common days repeat every LCM(3,4) = 12 days after day 2, so the next is day 14.

question: A single machine serves jobs in turns. Each turn lasts at most 3 minutes; a job that is not finished goes to the back of the queue. The queue at time 0 is A (needs 7 minutes), B (4), C (9), D (3), in that order. At what minute does job C finish?
why: Turns: A 0-3, B 3-6, C 6-9, D 9-12 (D done), A 12-15, B 15-16 (B done), C 16-19, A 19-20 (A done), C 20-23. C gets its last 3 minutes at 20-23, so it finishes at minute 23.

question: Tasks and durations in days: P 4, Q 3, R 5, S 2, T 3, U 2. Precedence: R needs P; S needs P and Q; T needs R; U needs S and T. Unlimited workers are available. By how many days can task S be delayed without delaying the whole project?
why: The project takes 14 days (P-R-T-U). S can start at day 4 (after P) and must end by day 12 (when U starts), so it has a window of 8 days for 2 days of work: 6 days of slack.

question: Four jobs must each pass through Machine 1 and then Machine 2 (a job starts on Machine 2 only after finishing on Machine 1 and when Machine 2 is free). Machine 1 times: J1 3, J2 5, J3 2, J4 4. Machine 2 times: J1 4, J2 2, J3 6, J4 3. Jobs go through each machine in the same order. What is the minimum time to complete all four jobs?
why: Put jobs that are quick on Machine 1 first and jobs that are quick on Machine 2 last (Johnson's rule): order J3, J1, J4, J2. Machine 1 ends at 14; Machine 2 runs 2-8 (J3), 8-12 (J1), 12-15 (J4), 15-17 (J2) = 17 minutes.

question: Three counters serve a queue of 8 customers who all arrive at time 0. Counter X takes 2 minutes per item, Counter Y takes 3 minutes per item and Counter Z takes 4 minutes per item. why: Simulate in order: C1 (2 items) to X: 0-4. C2 (1) to Y: 0-3. C3 (3) to Z: 0-12. C4 (2) to Y (free at 3): 3-9. C5 (1) to X (free at 4): 4-6. C6 (2) to X (free at 6): 6-10. C7 (3) to Y (free at 9): 9-18. C8 (1) to X (free at 10): 10-12. The last to finish is C7 at minute 18.

question: Six tasks with durations in hours: a 3, b 4, c 2, d 5, e 3, f 2. Precedence: d needs a; e needs b and c; f needs d and e. Only two workers are available, each can do one task at a time, and tasks cannot be split. What is the shortest time in which all tasks can be finished?
why: Task f needs both d and e. Best case d ends at hour 8 (a then d). For e to end by hour 8, b, c and e (9 hours of work) would all have to fit in 8 hours on the other worker, which is impossible. The best plan is worker 1: a, d; worker 2: b, c, e (ends at 9); then f from hour 9 to 11.

question: Free times (24-hour clock). Asha: 9:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:30. Bhaskar: 9:30-11:15 and 13:00-16:45. Chitra: 10:00-12:00 and 14:15-18:00. Dhruv: 8:00-11:30 and 14:30-17:00. All four must attend one meeting that needs an unbroken common slot. What is the longest unbroken slot (in minutes) when all four are free?
why: Intersect the lists: morning common time is 10:00-11:15 (75 min) and afternoon 14:30-16:45 (135 min). The longer unbroken slot is 135 minutes.

question: Roads between towns (distance of each direct road): Agra-Bhopal 2 km; Agra-Chennai 3 km; Bhopal-Chennai 2 km; Chennai-Delhi 9 km; Chennai-Indore 7 km; Delhi-Indore 8 km. What is the length of the shortest route from Agra to Delhi?
why: The shortest route is Agra-Chennai-Delhi with length 12 km; the other routes are longer.

question: Roads between towns (distance of each direct road): Agra-Bhopal 2 km; Agra-Chennai 3 km; Agra-Delhi 2 km; Bhopal-Chennai 2 km; Chennai-Delhi 9 km; Chennai-Indore 7 km; Delhi-Indore 8 km. What is the length of the shortest route from Bhopal to Indore?
why: The shortest route is Bhopal-Chennai-Indore with length 9 km; the other routes are longer.

question: A delivery rider moves on a city grid only east or north. To go from the depot to a customer who is 3 blocks east and 2 blocks north, how many different shortest routes are there?
why: Every shortest route has 3 east moves and 2 north moves in some order: 5!/(3!2!) = 10.

question: There are 3 different roads from Kota to Mysuru and 4 different roads from Mysuru to Nagpur. Without repeating any road, how many different routes lead from Kota to Nagpur via Mysuru?
why: Choose one road for each leg: 3 x 4 = 12.

question: A metro train takes 3 minutes between any two consecutive stations and stops for 1 minute at every station in between (not at the first or last station of the trip). Starting from Station 1, how long does it take to reach Station 6 on the same line?
why: There are 5 gaps of 3 minutes = 15, and 4 intermediate stops (Stations 2 to 5) of 1 minute = 4. Total 19 minutes.

question: From town P to town R you can go directly by bus for ₹90, or via town Q using a ₹35 bus from P to Q, a ₹40 bus from Q to R and a ₹10 platform fee at Q. Which option is cheaper, and by how much?
why: Via Q: 35 + 40 + 10 = ₹85. Direct is ₹90, so via Q is ₹5 cheaper.

question: Roads between towns (distance of each direct road): Jaipur-Kota 8 km; Jaipur-Lucknow 3 km; Jaipur-Nagpur 2 km; Kota-Mysuru 8 km; Kota-Ooty 5 km; Lucknow-Mysuru 9 km; Lucknow-Nagpur 8 km; Mysuru-Ooty 8 km. What is the length of the shortest route from Jaipur to Ooty?
why: The shortest route is Jaipur-Kota-Ooty with length 13 km; the other routes are longer.

question: Roads between towns (distance of each direct road): Jaipur-Kota 8 km; Jaipur-Lucknow 3 km; Jaipur-Nagpur 2 km; Kota-Mysuru 8 km; Kota-Ooty 5 km; Lucknow-Mysuru 9 km; Lucknow-Nagpur 8 km; Mysuru-Ooty 8 km; Nagpur-Ooty 2 km. What is the length of the shortest route from Kota to Nagpur?
why: The shortest route is Kota-Ooty-Nagpur with length 7 km; the other routes are longer.

question: On a city grid a rider moves only east or north from the start (0,0) to the destination (5,3). She must pass through the market at (2,1). How many different shortest routes are there?
why: Start to market: 2 east + 1 north = C(3,1) = 3 routes. Market to destination: 3 east + 2 north = C(5,2) = 10 routes. Total 3 x 10 = 30. Unrestricted there would be C(8,3) = 56.

question: Metro Line 1 and Line 2 meet at Central. A Line 1 train takes 18 minutes from Aarey to Central. Line 2 trains leave Central every 10 minutes starting at 8:00 (8:00, 8:10, 8:20 and so on) and take 12 minutes from Central to Dock. Priya boards a Line 1 train at Aarey at 8:02. Changing platforms takes 4 minutes. At what time does she reach Dock?
why: She reaches Central at 8:20, and is ready for Line 2 at 8:24. The next Line 2 train leaves at 8:30 and reaches Dock 12 minutes later, at 8:42.

question: Four ways to travel between two cities: Direct bus (₹130, 4 hours), Train + auto (₹90, 6 hours), Flight (₹250, 2 hours) and Bus + train (₹70, 9 hours). Sneha must arrive within 6 hours and wants the lowest cost. Which option should she choose?
why: Options within 6 hours: Direct bus, Train + auto, Flight. The cheapest of these is Train + auto at ₹90. Bus + train is cheaper but takes 9 hours.

question: Roads between towns (distance of each direct road): Jaipur-Kota 8 km; Jaipur-Lucknow 3 km; Jaipur-Nagpur 2 km; Kota-Mysuru 8 km; Kota-Ooty 5 km; Lucknow-Mysuru 9 km; Lucknow-Nagpur 8 km; Mysuru-Ooty 8 km; Nagpur-Ooty 2 km. A courier must go from Jaipur to Ooty and must pass through Lucknow on the way, without visiting any town twice. What is the shortest possible distance?
why: Only routes through Lucknow count. The best is Jaipur-Lucknow-Nagpur-Ooty with length 13 km. The overall shortest route (4 km) does not pass Lucknow.

question: Roads between towns (distance of each direct road): Pune-Surat 7 km; Pune-Thane 8 km; Pune-Vapi 5 km; Pune-Wardha 5 km; Raipur-Udaipur 9 km; Surat-Thane 9 km; Surat-Udaipur 2 km; Thane-Wardha 9 km; Udaipur-Wardha 5 km; Vapi-Wardha 5 km. A route may not visit a town twice. The shortest route from Pune to Wardha is the first choice. What is the length of the second shortest route (a different route with the next larger total length)?
why: Listing all routes: shortest is Pune-Wardha (5 km) and the next is Pune-Vapi-Wardha (10 km).

question: A rider moves only east or north on a grid from (0,0) to (5,4). Two junctions, (2,2) and (3,1), are flooded and cannot be used. How many different shortest routes remain?
why: Unrestricted: C(9,4) = 126. Through (2,2): C(4,2) x C(5,3) = 6 x 10 = 60. Through (3,1): C(4,1) x C(5,2) = 4 x 10 = 40. No route can use both flooded junctions, so 126 - 60 - 40 = 26.

question: Line A trains leave Origin every 12 minutes starting at 6:00 and take 25 minutes to reach Hub. Line B trains leave Hub every 15 minutes starting at 6:05 and take 20 minutes to reach Destination. Walking between the Line A and Line B platforms at Hub takes 5 minutes. Rahul reaches Origin at 7:10 and boards the first Line A train he can. At what time does he reach Destination?
why: Line A departs at 6:00, 6:12, ... so the first train at or after 7:10 leaves at 7:12 and reaches Hub at 7:37. After the walk he is ready at 7:42. Line B departs at 6:05, 6:20, ...; the first at or after 7:42 is 7:50, arriving at 8:10.

question: Bus services between towns (fare, travel time): Jaipur-Lucknow ₹70, 1 h; Jaipur-Mysuru ₹20, 4 h; Jaipur-Nagpur ₹20, 3 h; Kota-Nagpur ₹60, 3 h; Kota-Ooty ₹80, 1 h; Lucknow-Mysuru ₹70, 4 h; Lucknow-Nagpur ₹20, 3 h; Mysuru-Ooty ₹20, 4 h; Nagpur-Ooty ₹70, 4 h. A traveller goes from Jaipur to Ooty, visiting no town twice, and must finish within 7 hours of travel. What is the lowest total fare?
why: Listing all routes: the cheapest overall (₹40) takes more than 7 hours. The cheapest route within the limit is Jaipur-Nagpur-Ooty at ₹90 taking 7 hours.

question: Roads between towns (distance of each direct road): Pune-Surat 7 km; Pune-Thane 8 km; Pune-Vapi 5 km; Pune-Wardha 5 km; Raipur-Udaipur 9 km; Surat-Thane 9 km; Surat-Udaipur 2 km; Thane-Wardha 9 km; Udaipur-Wardha 5 km; Vapi-Wardha 5 km. A van starts at Pune, must visit Raipur, Surat and Thane (in any order, passing through other towns if needed) and returns to Pune. What is the shortest total distance?
why: Try each order of the three stops using shortest distances between towns. The best order is Pune, Raipur, Surat, Thane, Pune with 46 km.

question: Roads between towns (distance of each direct road): Pune-Surat 7 km; Pune-Thane 8 km; Pune-Vapi 5 km; Pune-Wardha 5 km; Raipur-Udaipur 9 km; Surat-Thane 9 km; Surat-Udaipur 2 km; Thane-Wardha 9 km; Udaipur-Wardha 5 km; Vapi-Wardha 5 km. The shortest route from Pune to Wardha is used daily. Which single road, if closed, would lengthen the shortest route the most?
why: The shortest route is the direct Pune-Wardha road (5 km). Closing it forces the next best route, Pune-Vapi-Wardha (10 km). Closing any other road leaves the 5 km road available, so the distance does not change.

question: In a class of 60 students, 35 play cricket, 30 play football and 10 play both. How many students play neither game?
why: At least one game: 35 + 30 - 10 = 55. Neither: 60 - 55 = 5.

question: In a group of 80 people, 50 read The Hindu, 40 read Times of India and 15 read both. How many read only The Hindu?
why: Only The Hindu = 50 - 15 = 35.

question: 70% of the people in a town drink tea and 60% drink coffee. Everyone drinks at least one of the two. What percentage drink both?
In a group of 60 people, 40 like tea and 35 like coffee. What is the least possible number who like both?
why: Tea + coffee = 75 which exceeds 60 by 15. These 15 must overlap, so at least 15 like both.

question: Of 120 employees, 70 know Hindi, 55 know Tamil and 20 know neither. How many know both languages?
why: Know at least one: 120 - 20 = 100. Both = 70 + 55 - 100 = 25.

question: In a club of 100 members, 45 play chess, 30 play carrom and 12 play both. How many members play exactly one of the two games?
why: Chess only = 45 - 12 = 33, carrom only = 30 - 12 = 18. Exactly one = 33 + 18 = 51.

question: In a survey of 100 people, 50 like A, 45 like B and 40 like C. 20 like both A and B, 15 like both A and C and 10 like both B and C. 95 like at least one of the three. How many like all three?
why: |A U B U C| = 50 + 45 + 40 - 20 - 15 - 10 + all three = 90 + all three. This equals 95, so all three = 5.

question: In a survey of 100 people, everyone likes at least one of three fruits: mango (50 people), apple (45) and banana (40). Exactly 10 people like all three. How many like exactly two of the fruits?
why: Let x = people liking exactly one and y = exactly two. x + y + 10 = 100, and x + 2y + 3(10) = 50 + 45 + 40 = 135. Subtracting: y + 20 = 35, so y = 15.

question: Of 120 students, 60 study Maths, 50 study Physics and 45 study Chemistry. 20 study both Maths and Physics, 15 study both Maths and Chemistry, 10 study both Physics and Chemistry, and 5 study all three. How many study none of the three?
In a group of 200 people, 60% own a car and 70% own a bike. What is the greatest possible number of people who own both?
why: The overlap cannot exceed the smaller group: 60% of 200 = 120. This is reached when every car owner also owns a bike.

question: Of 120 students, 60 study Maths, 50 study Physics and 45 study Chemistry. 20 study both Maths and Physics, 15 study both Maths and Chemistry, and 5 study all three. How many study Maths only?
why: Maths only = 60 - (20 + 15 - 5) = 60 - 30 = 30. The 5 who study all three are counted in both overlaps, so they are added back once.

question: In a company, 45% of the employees know Python and 35% know SQL. 20% know both. What percentage know neither?
In a group of 20 people, 14 like tea, 15 like coffee and 16 like juice. What is the least possible number of people who like all three drinks?
why: People who do not like a drink: 6 (tea), 5 (coffee), 4 (juice) = 15 at most. So at least 20 - 15 = 5 people like all three.

question: Everyone in a group of 20 likes at least one of tea (14 people), coffee (15) and juice (16). What is the greatest possible number of people who like exactly one of the three drinks?
why: Let x like exactly one, y exactly two and z all three. x + y + z = 20 and x + 2y + 3z = 45. Subtracting gives y + 2z = 25, so x = z - 5. Since y = 25 - 2z cannot be negative, z is at most 12, so x is at most 7.

question: Everyone in a group of 20 likes at least one of tea (14 people), coffee (15) and juice (16). What is the greatest possible number of people who like exactly two of the drinks?
why: With x, y, z as before, y + 2z = 25 and z is at least 5 (the least possible number liking all three), so y = 25 - 2z is at most 25 - 10 = 15.

question: Of 100 people, 60 own a TV, 50 own a fridge and 40 own an AC. 25 own both TV and fridge, 20 own both TV and AC, and 15 own both fridge and AC (these pair counts include people who own all three). 5 people own none of the three. How many own exactly two of the three items?
why: At least one item: 95. 60 + 50 + 40 - 25 - 20 - 15 + z = 95 gives 90 + z = 95, so z = 5 own all three. Pair counts total 25 + 20 + 15 = 60 and count the triple-owners 3 times, so exactly two = 60 - 3 x 5 = 45.

question: In a group of 20 people, 14 like tea, 15 like coffee and 16 like juice. What is the greatest possible number of people who like none of the three drinks?
why: The people who like none must lie outside the largest group (juice, 16), so at most 20 - 16 = 4. This is possible when the tea and coffee lovers are all inside the juice group.

question: Everyone in a group of 20 likes at least one of tea (14 people), coffee (15) and juice (16). What is the least possible number of people who like at least two of the three drinks?
why: Using y + 2z = 25 (y exactly two, z all three) the number liking at least two is y + z = 25 - z. This is smallest when z is largest. z cannot exceed 12 (otherwise y is negative), so the least is 25 - 12 = 13.

question: The sum of the ages of a father and his son is 48 years. The father is 3 times as old as the son. How old will the son be after 6 years?
why: Son + 3 x son = 48, so the son is 12 now. After 6 years he will be 18.

question: Plan A charges ₹300 a month plus ₹2 per minute of calls. Plan B charges ₹150 a month plus ₹3 per minute. For how many minutes of calls in a month do both plans cost the same?
why: Plan A - Plan B fixed fee difference is ₹150, and B costs ₹1 more per minute: 150/1 = 150 minutes.

question: An electricity board charges ₹3 per unit for the first 100 units, ₹5 per unit for the next 100 units and ₹7 per unit beyond 200 units. What is the bill for 250 units?
Asha invests ₹40,000 and Bela invests ₹60,000 in a business for one year. They earn a profit of ₹50,000. What is Asha's share of the profit?
why: The investments are in the ratio 2 : 3, so Asha gets 2/5 of 50,000 = ₹20,000.

question: The sum of two numbers is 45 and their difference is 9. What is the larger number?
₹1,200 is shared among three friends in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7. How much does the friend with the smallest share get?
why: Total parts = 12, one part = ₹100, smallest share = 2 parts = ₹200.

question: Five years ago a father was 5 times as old as his son. Ten years from now he will be twice as old as his son. How old is the father now?
why: Let the son be s now. Father now = 5(s - 5) + 5 = 5s - 20. In 10 years: 5s - 10 = 2(s + 10), so s = 10 and the father is 30.

question: A broadband company offers three plans. Basic: ₹200 fixed plus ₹4 per GB. Plus: ₹500 fixed plus ₹2 per GB. Max: ₹900 fixed plus ₹1 per GB. A family uses 250 GB in a month. Which plan is cheapest and what does it cost?

An income tax has these slabs: nothing on the first ₹3,00,000; 5% on the next ₹3,00,000; 10% on the next ₹3,00,000; and 15% on any income above ₹9,00,000. How much tax is payable on an income of ₹11,00,000?
why: 5% of 3,00,000 = 15,000; 10% of 3,00,000 = 30,000; 15% of the remaining 2,00,000 = 30,000. Total ₹75,000. Applying 15% to the whole income would wrongly give ₹1,65,000.

question: Anil puts ₹50,000 into a business for 12 months, Bela puts ₹80,000 for 6 months and Charu puts ₹60,000 for 8 months. They share a profit of ₹1,56,000 in proportion to money x time. How much does Charu get?
why: Money x months: Anil 6,00,000; Bela 4,80,000; Charu 4,80,000. Ratio 5 : 4 : 4, so Charu gets 4/13 of 1,56,000 = ₹48,000.

question: The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 90. What is the largest of the three?
why: The middle number is 90/3 = 30, so the numbers are 28, 30 and 32. The largest is 32.

question: A taxi charges ₹40 for the first 2 km, ₹12 per km for the next 8 km, and ₹15 per km beyond 10 km. Waiting costs ₹2 per minute. What is the fare for a 14 km trip with 10 minutes of waiting?
An electricity board charges ₹3 per unit for the first 100 units, ₹5 per unit for the next 100 units and ₹7 per unit beyond 200 units. A household's bill was ₹1,850. How many units did it use?
why: The first 200 units cost 300 + 500 = ₹800. The remaining ₹1,050 at ₹7 buys 150 units. Total 350 units.

question: Three data plans: P costs ₹400 plus ₹3 per GB. Q costs ₹250 plus ₹5 per GB. R costs a flat ₹1,000 for up to 150 GB, and ₹6 for each GB beyond 150. For how many whole-number values of monthly usage (in GB) is Q strictly the cheapest of the three?
why: Q beats P when 250 + 5x < 400 + 3x, i.e. x < 75 (x up to 74). Q beats R when 250 + 5x < 1000, i.e. x < 150. Both hold for x = 0 to 74, so 75 values.

question: Asha starts a business with ₹1,00,000. After 4 months she withdraws ₹20,000. Bela starts with ₹80,000 and after 6 months adds ₹40,000. At the end of the year (12 months) the profit is ₹1,68,000, shared in proportion to money x time. How much does Asha get?
A two-digit number is 4 times the sum of its digits. When its digits are reversed, the new number is 27 more than the original. What is the original number?
why: Numbers equal to 4 x digit sum: 12, 24, 36, 48. Reversals add 9, 18, 27 and 36 respectively, so only 36 (reversed 63) works.

question: Four friends' present ages add up to 74 years. Ravi is 4 years older than Sam. Tina is half as old as Ravi. After 5 years Uma will be exactly twice as old as Sam will be then. How old is Uma now?
A salesperson earns 5% commission on the first ₹2,00,000 of monthly sales, 8% on the next ₹3,00,000 and 12% on sales beyond ₹5,00,000. What monthly sales give her a commission of ₹46,000?
why: The first ₹5,00,000 earns 10,000 + 24,000 = ₹34,000. The remaining ₹12,000 at 12% needs ₹1,00,000 more sales. Total ₹6,00,000.
